name: 8. Testing and QA
description: Strategy, unit and e2e tests, coverage, performance, accessibility.

cards.subject: A unit test
says: checks a small piece of logic in isolation
runs in milliseconds because it needs no network or real database
cards.use: want fast feedback on the rules inside one function
not: needs a fully deployed environment to run

cards.subject: An integration test
says: checks that several parts work together, such as code and a real database
catches wiring and configuration mistakes that isolated tests cannot see
cards.use: need to confirm that a query really runs against the database
not: is always faster than a unit test

cards.subject: An end-to-end test
says: drives the whole application through its real user interface
sits at the top of the pyramid and is kept to a small number
cards.use: need proof that a critical journey such as sign-up works from browser to database
not: is the cheapest way to pinpoint which function is broken

cards.subject: A contract test
says: checks that a consumer and a provider agree on the shape of requests and responses
lets two services be verified separately without a shared full environment
cards.use: want to catch a breaking API change before the provider is deployed
not: replaces all testing inside each service

cards.subject: A smoke test
says: runs a small set of checks to see whether a build is basically alive
stops deeper testing early when it fails
cards.use: need a quick check right after a deploy that the app starts and the main page loads
not: covers every feature in depth

cards.subject: An acceptance test
says: checks that a feature meets the agreed business requirement
is often phrased in the customer's own terms
cards.use: need to confirm that a feature does what the stakeholder asked for
not: checks only the internal structure of the code

cards.subject: A component test
says: exercises one module or service through its public interface with its dependencies replaced
sits between unit and integration in scope
cards.use: want to test a whole service in-process without the network

cards.subject: A snapshot test
says: compares current output with a stored earlier output and fails on any difference
needs a person to review the stored output when it changes on purpose
cards.use: need to notice unintended changes in rendered markup or serialised data
not: proves the stored output was correct when it was first recorded

cards.subject: A system test
says: verifies the complete integrated product against its specified requirements, not one part
is run on a full build before acceptance
cards.use: need to verify the whole integrated build against its requirements before acceptance

cards.subject: The test pyramid
says: puts many unit tests at the base and few end-to-end tests at the top
trades realism for speed and low cost as you move down
cards.use: need a simple shape for balancing fast and realistic tests
not: says end-to-end tests should outnumber unit tests

cards.subject: A test strategy
says: describes the overall approach to testing, including levels and what blocks a release
says what is deliberately not tested and why
cards.use: need a shared answer to what we test, at what level and what blocks a release

cards.subject: A test plan
says: details the scope, schedule, resources and risks of one testing effort
lists the entry and exit criteria for that effort
cards.use: need to organise who tests what, and when, for one release

cards.subject: Risk-based testing
says: puts the most testing effort where a failure would cost the most
ranks areas by the likelihood and impact of failure
cards.use: have limited time and must choose what to test first
not: spreads effort equally across every feature

cards.subject: Shift-left testing
says: moves testing earlier in the lifecycle, such as reviewing requirements and running tests on every commit
lowers the cost of fixing defects by finding them sooner
cards.use: want defects found while they are still cheap to fix

cards.subject: Entry criteria
says: are conditions that must hold before testing can start, such as a stable build and a ready environment
stop a team wasting effort on a build that cannot run
cards.use: need to agree when QA may begin testing a build

cards.subject: Exit criteria
says: are conditions that must hold before testing can be declared complete
often include no open critical defects and an agreed pass rate
cards.use: need a clear definition of done for a test cycle

cards.subject: A test summary report
says: summarises what was tested, the results, open defects and risks at the end of a cycle
gives decision makers evidence about release readiness
cards.use: need to tell stakeholders how testing went

cards.subject: A go/no-go decision
says: is the explicit call, made with stakeholders, on whether to ship given the test evidence and risks
may knowingly accept some open issues
cards.use: need an accountable decision on shipping a release candidate

cards.subject: A known issues list
says: records defects that ship unfixed, with their impact and any workaround
means open problems are accepted knowingly rather than discovered by customers
cards.use: must ship with defects that will not be fixed in time

cards.subject: A rollback plan
says: describes how to return to the previous working version if a release goes wrong
is prepared and checked before the release, not after the failure
cards.use: want a safe way back if a deployment misbehaves

cards.subject: A release candidate
says: is a build believed ready to ship that is tested as it is
is promoted unchanged if it passes and replaced only if a blocking defect is found
cards.use: need to be sure that what was tested is exactly what ships
like: Building once and promoting the same artifact

cards.subject: A canary release
says: sends a new version to a small share of traffic before everyone gets it
limits how many users are hurt by a defect that escaped testing
cards.use: want real-traffic evidence before a full rollout
not: removes the need for any pre-release testing

cards.subject: A feature flag
says: lets code ship switched off and be enabled later without a new deploy
allows a misbehaving feature to be turned off quickly
cards.use: want to separate deploying code from releasing a feature
not: removes the need to test both the on and off paths

cards.subject: Equivalence partitioning
says: divides inputs into classes expected to behave the same
tests one representative value from each class
cards.use: want to cut a huge input range down to a few representative cases
not: tests every possible input value

cards.subject: Boundary value analysis
says: tests values at and next to the edges of each input range
targets off-by-one errors such as writing < where <= was meant
cards.use: need to test a field that accepts values from 1 to 100
not: picks only values from the middle of each range

cards.subject: Decision table testing
says: lists combinations of conditions with the action expected for each
suits rules where several conditions together decide the outcome
cards.use: have business rules such as eligibility that combine several yes or no conditions

cards.subject: State transition testing
says: models the system as states and the events that move between them
finds invalid transitions such as paying for an already cancelled order
cards.use: need to test a workflow whose behaviour depends on its current state

cards.subject: Pairwise testing
says: covers every pair of parameter values in at least one test
cuts the number of combinations while still catching failures caused by two parameters interacting
cards.use: face too many combinations of browser, operating system and setting to run them all
not: guarantees finding every defect that needs three parameters to interact

cards.subject: Error guessing
says: uses the tester's experience of common mistakes to choose cases
tries things like empty input, very long strings and special characters
cards.use: want to use past defects to aim extra cases at likely weak spots

cards.subject: Exploratory testing
says: combines learning, test design and execution at the same time
relies on the tester's skill and curiosity rather than pre-written steps
cards.use: need to find problems nobody thought to write a script for
not: means clicking at random without taking any notes

cards.subject: Session-based test management
says: structures exploratory testing into time-boxed sessions with a charter and notes
ends each session with a short debrief
cards.use: want exploratory testing that can be planned and reported

cards.subject: A test charter
says: states the mission of one exploratory session, such as exploring checkout with declined cards
gives focus without prescribing every step
cards.use: need to point an exploratory session at one area

cards.subject: Property-based testing
says: checks that a stated property holds for many generated inputs
shrinks a failing input to a minimal example
cards.use: want to find edge cases you would never have written by hand
not: replaces every example-based test with a fixed list of inputs

cards.subject: A dummy
says: fills a required parameter and is never actually used
needs no behaviour at all
cards.use: must pass an argument that the code under test never touches

cards.subject: A stub
says: returns canned answers to calls made by the code under test
lets a test control indirect inputs such as a fixed exchange rate
cards.use: need a dependency to return a fixed value so the test is repeatable
not: fails the test when it is not called

cards.subject: A spy
says: records how it was called so the test can inspect the calls afterwards
can wrap a real object while still observing it
cards.use: want to check afterwards what arguments a collaborator received

cards.subject: A mock
says: is given expectations about calls and fails the test if they are not met
verifies behaviour such as an email being sent exactly once
cards.use: need to verify that the code told a collaborator to do something
not: contains a full working implementation

cards.subject: A fake
says: has a real but simplified working implementation, such as an in-memory database
is too lightweight for production yet behaves realistically
cards.use: want a quick stand-in that actually stores and returns data
not: only returns hard-coded values

cards.subject: Service virtualisation
says: simulates the behaviour of a whole remote system, including latency and error responses
lets testing go on when the real dependency is unavailable or costly
cards.use: must test against a third-party system that has no usable sandbox

cards.subject: A recorded HTTP fixture
says: replays responses captured earlier from the real service
goes stale if the real API changes, so it needs refreshing
cards.use: want realistic responses without calling the live service on every run

cards.subject: Test-driven development
says: writes a failing test before the code that makes it pass
repeats a red, green, refactor cycle
cards.use: want small tests to drive a testable design
not: writes all tests after the feature is finished

cards.subject: Behaviour-driven development
says: describes behaviour in a plain-language format that business people and developers both read
turns examples into executable specifications
cards.use: want requirements, tests and documentation to share one readable form

cards.subject: Acceptance test-driven development
says: writes acceptance tests with the customer before the feature is built
uses those tests as the definition of done for the story
cards.use: want the customer's examples to decide when a story is finished

cards.subject: Regression testing
says: reruns existing tests to confirm that a change broke nothing that used to work
grows from bugs when each fix gets a test of its own
cards.use: have just changed code and need to be sure old behaviour still works
not: tests only brand new features

cards.subject: Arrange-Act-Assert
says: structures a test into setup, one action and then checks
keeps each test focused on a single behaviour
cards.use: want unit tests that read the same way every time

cards.subject: Given-When-Then
says: writes a scenario as a context, an event and an expected outcome in business language
is the scenario structure used by Gherkin in BDD
cards.use: need a scenario format that a non-programmer can review
not: is only usable for tests of private methods

cards.subject: Test isolation
says: keeps each test independent so it can run alone or in any order
gives each test its own data instead of sharing state
cards.use: see tests that pass alone but fail when the whole suite runs

cards.subject: A parameterised test
says: runs the same test logic over a table of inputs and expected outputs
reports each row as a separate case
cards.use: have many boundary cases that differ only in their data

cards.subject: A characterisation test
says: records what legacy code currently does, right or wrong
gives a safety net before refactoring code that has no tests
cards.use: must change untested legacy code and first need to know what it does

cards.subject: A test oracle
says: is the source of truth used to decide whether an output is correct
can be a specification, a reference implementation or an independent calculation
cards.use: need an independent way to know the expected answer

cards.subject: Testability
says: describes how easily software can be put into a state and observed in a test
improves when dependencies are injected rather than created inside the code
cards.use: find code that cannot be tested without a real network or clock

cards.subject: Load testing
says: applies the expected volume of concurrent users to measure response times and errors
checks behaviour at the traffic the system is meant to carry
cards.use: need to know whether the site stays fast with the user numbers you expect

cards.subject: Stress testing
says: pushes the system beyond its expected capacity to find where and how it fails
checks that it fails gracefully and recovers afterwards
cards.use: want to find the breaking point of a service

cards.subject: Soak testing
says: runs a steady load for many hours to expose slow leaks such as growing memory
finds problems that appear only over time
cards.use: suspect a memory leak that shows up only after days

cards.subject: Spike testing
says: applies a sudden large jump in traffic and then drops it
checks how well the system absorbs and recovers from bursts
cards.use: expect a promotional email to send a burst of visitors at one moment

cards.subject: Usability testing
says: watches real users attempt tasks to find confusion and friction
measures how easy a product is to learn and use
cards.use: need to know whether people can actually complete a task in the interface

cards.subject: Compatibility testing
says: checks behaviour across browsers, devices, operating systems and versions
uses the platforms your real users have to decide what to cover
cards.use: need to confirm the site works on the browsers your users have

cards.subject: Visual regression testing
says: compares screenshots of rendered pages with approved baselines
flags unintended layout and styling changes that functional assertions miss
cards.use: worry that a CSS change moved or hid something without any test failing

cards.subject: Chaos testing
says: injects failures such as killed instances or slow dependencies on purpose
checks that resilience mechanisms work in practice, not only on paper
cards.use: want evidence that the system survives an instance dying

cards.subject: Recovery testing
says: forces a crash or outage and checks that the system comes back with its data intact
validates backup restore and failover procedures
cards.use: need proof that a backup can really be restored

cards.subject: Keyboard-only navigation
says: checks that every control can be reached and used without a mouse
exposes missing focus handling and keyboard traps
cards.use: want a quick first accessibility check with no tools

cards.subject: A colour contrast check
says: measures text colour against its background against a required ratio
helps users with low vision read content
cards.use: worry that grey text on a white page is hard to read

cards.subject: Alt text on images
says: gives a meaningful description of an image so a screen reader can convey it
is left empty for purely decorative images
cards.use: need a screen reader user to understand a chart or photo

cards.subject: A screen reader pass
says: walks key journeys with assistive technology to hear what users actually get
finds problems that automated scanners cannot detect
cards.use: want to know what a blind user experiences on the checkout flow

cards.subject: An automated accessibility scan
says: flags rule violations such as missing alt text or low contrast
detects only a portion of real accessibility problems
cards.use: want fast accessibility checks on every pull request
not: proves a page is fully accessible when it reports zero issues

cards.subject: A focus order check
says: verifies that tab order follows the visual and logical reading order
includes moving focus into and back out of dialogs
cards.use: see keyboard focus jump around the page unpredictably

cards.subject: aria-hidden on decorative graphics
says: hides decorative content from assistive technology
suits icons whose meaning is already given by nearby text
cards.use: want a screen reader to skip a purely decorative SVG
not: should be put on the main call-to-action button so it is read twice

cards.subject: aria-label on icon-only buttons
says: gives a button with no visible text an accessible name
is read by a screen reader instead of nothing
cards.use: have a button showing only an icon that a screen reader announces as just button

cards.subject: Static application security testing
says: analyses source code without running it to find vulnerability patterns
can run early, even before the app can be built
cards.use: want security findings on every commit before deployment
not: needs a running application to probe

cards.subject: Dynamic application security testing
says: probes a running application from the outside like an attacker
finds issues that appear only at runtime, such as misconfigured headers
cards.use: need to test a deployed staging site for runtime weaknesses

cards.subject: Dependency vulnerability scanning
says: checks third-party libraries against lists of known vulnerabilities
flags outdated packages that have published advisories
cards.use: worry that a library you depend on has a known security hole

cards.subject: Secret scanning
says: searches code and history for committed keys, tokens and passwords
can block a push that contains a credential
cards.use: want to stop an API key reaching the repository

cards.subject: A penetration test
says: has a skilled tester actively attempt to exploit the system within an agreed scope
chains weaknesses together the way a real attacker would
cards.use: want a human attacker's view of how far an intruder could get

cards.subject: Fuzzing
says: feeds large volumes of malformed or random input to find crashes and hangs
finds parser and input-handling bugs people did not think to test
cards.use: need to harden a file or protocol parser against hostile input

cards.subject: An authorisation test
says: verifies that a user cannot act beyond their role, such as a manager offboarding an admin
checks that the server enforces permissions and not just the interface hiding buttons
cards.use: need to prove one role cannot perform another role's actions

cards.subject: An input validation test
says: sends hostile or malformed input such as script tags and SQL fragments
confirms the application rejects or safely encodes it
cards.use: want to see how a form handles a script tag typed into a text field

cards.subject: Severity
says: measures the technical or user impact of a defect
is set by what the defect does, not by when it must be fixed
cards.use: need to describe how badly a bug hurts the system
not: decides the order in which bugs are scheduled

cards.subject: Priority
says: sets the order in which defects should be fixed
reflects business urgency and can differ from severity
cards.use: need to decide which bug the team fixes first
not: is always the same as severity

cards.subject: A bug report
says: records a defect with a clear title, expected result, actual result and environment
lets someone else understand what went wrong without asking
cards.use: have found a defect and must hand it to a developer

cards.subject: Reproduction steps
says: list the exact ordered actions and data that trigger the defect
turn a vague complaint into something a developer can debug
cards.use: hear a customer say it sometimes breaks and need to make it repeatable

cards.subject: The defect lifecycle
says: tracks a defect through states such as new, assigned, fixed, verified and closed
may reopen a defect when the fix fails verification
cards.use: need to know what state a bug is in and who owns it next

cards.subject: Bug triage
says: reviews new defects to confirm, prioritise and assign them
decides which defects will not be fixed
cards.use: have a pile of new reports and need to sort them

cards.subject: Root cause analysis
says: asks why a defect happened, not just what it is
aims to prevent the whole class of problem, for example with a new check
cards.use: keep seeing the same kind of bug after fixes

cards.subject: An escaped defect
says: is a defect found by customers or in production rather than by testing
prompts the question of which test would have caught it
cards.use: learn about a bug from a customer complaint

cards.subject: Confirmation testing
says: reruns the exact failing case to confirm that a fix worked
differs from regression testing, which checks that nothing else broke
cards.use: have a fix for a bug and need to verify the fix itself

cards.subject: Defect clustering
says: observes that a small number of modules tend to contain most of the defects
suggests concentrating extra testing on those areas
cards.use: notice that most bugs come from one old module

cards.subject: Line coverage
says: reports the percentage of code lines executed by tests
says nothing about whether those lines were checked by assertions
cards.use: need to see which lines no test ever runs
not: proves the tested lines are correct

cards.subject: Branch coverage
says: reports whether each outcome of every decision, true and false, was taken
is stricter than line coverage
cards.use: want to know whether the else paths are ever tested

cards.subject: Mutation score
says: is the share of deliberately injected code changes that the tests detect
exposes tests that run code without checking its result
cards.use: doubt that high coverage means the tests would catch real bugs

cards.subject: Defect escape rate
says: is the share of defects found after release rather than before
indicates how many defects testing let through to customers
cards.use: want to judge how effective testing has been over several releases

cards.subject: Flaky rate
says: is the share of runs that fail then pass on rerun with no code change
shows how far a suite can be trusted
cards.use: want to know how much people can trust red builds

cards.subject: p95 latency
says: is the response time that 95 percent of requests beat
reveals slow tails that an average hides
cards.use: find that the average response time looks fine but some users still complain

cards.subject: Requirements coverage
says: is the share of requirements that have at least one test
finds untested features that code coverage cannot show
cards.use: want to know whether any specified feature has no test at all

cards.subject: Throughput
says: is the number of requests or transactions handled per unit of time
usually flattens or drops once a system saturates
cards.use: need to know how many orders per second the system can process

cards.subject: Test suite duration
says: is the time developers wait for feedback from the whole suite
grows until people stop running tests before merging unless it is managed
cards.use: find developers skipping tests because the run is slow

cards.subject: Test data
says: is the input and starting state that a test needs to run
should be created by the test or its setup, not left over from earlier runs
cards.use: need known inputs and records so a test is repeatable

cards.subject: A fixture
says: sets up a known starting state before a test and cleans up after
can be shared by tests that need the same setup
cards.use: have many tests that start from the same prepared state

cards.subject: A test data builder
says: creates valid objects with sensible defaults and lets a test override only the fields it cares about
keeps tests readable when entities have many required fields
cards.use: find tests cluttered with long lists of irrelevant required fields

cards.subject: Seed data
says: is a base set of records loaded into a database so it is usable
gives environments a predictable starting content
cards.use: want every fresh environment to start with the same reference records

cards.subject: Data masking
says: replaces sensitive values in copied production data with realistic stand-ins
lets testers use production-shaped data without exposing personal information
cards.use: want production-shaped data in a test environment without exposing real people

cards.subject: Synthetic data
says: is generated artificially instead of copied from real people
avoids privacy risk because no real record is involved
cards.use: need large volumes of realistic records but must not use real customers

cards.subject: A staging environment
says: is a production-like place to verify a release before it goes live
reduces but cannot remove differences from production
cards.use: want a final rehearsal of a release before customers see it

cards.subject: An ephemeral environment
says: is created for one branch or pull request and destroyed afterwards
avoids testers queuing for one shared environment
cards.use: want each pull request tested in its own clean copy of the app

cards.subject: Environment drift
says: is the gradual divergence of a test environment's configuration from production
lets a release pass in staging and still fail in production
cards.use: see a release that passed staging break on a setting that differs in production

cards.subject: Per-test transaction rollback
says: wraps each database test in a transaction that is undone at the end
keeps a shared test database clean without slow rebuilds
cards.use: want database tests isolated without recreating the schema each time

cards.subject: Shared mutable state
says: lets one test change data that another test then reads
makes results depend on what ran before
cards.use: find a test that passes alone but fails after another test

cards.subject: Order dependence
says: makes a test pass only when it runs after one particular other test
shows up when the suite is shuffled
cards.use: see failures appear after the runner starts randomising test order

cards.subject: Fixed sleep waits
says: pause for a set time and hope the page or service is ready
fail on a slow machine and waste time on a fast one
cards.use: find a browser test that sleeps two seconds before each check

cards.subject: Real clock dependence
says: makes results change with the time of day, the date or the timezone
is removed by injecting a controllable clock
cards.use: see a test fail only just after midnight or at the end of a month

cards.subject: Unseeded randomness
says: produces different inputs each run so a failure cannot be repeated
is controlled by fixing or logging the seed
cards.use: cannot reproduce a failure because the generated data differed

cards.subject: Live network dependence
says: lets a test fail because a real external service is slow or down
is avoided by replacing the service with a stub or fake
cards.use: see a test fail whenever a third-party API has a bad afternoon

cards.subject: An async race condition
says: occurs when a test checks a result before an asynchronous operation has finished
passes or fails depending on which side finishes first
cards.use: see an assertion run before a promise or callback completes

cards.subject: Resource contention in parallel runs
says: occurs when parallel tests fight over the same port, file or database row
appears only after the suite is split across workers
cards.use: see failures that appear only after tests are run in parallel

cards.subject: Fail-fast pipeline ordering
says: runs the cheapest, fastest checks first
stops the pipeline at the first failure to save time
cards.use: want developers to hear about a typo in seconds, not after a long suite

cards.subject: A quality gate
says: blocks a merge or release when defined checks fail
turns agreed standards into an automatic pass or fail
cards.use: want standards enforced by the pipeline rather than by memory
not: only warns and lets the pipeline continue

cards.subject: A required status check
says: is a branch protection rule that stops merging until named checks pass
stops a merge even when reviewers have approved it
cards.use: want a pull request unmergeable while the test job is red

cards.subject: Test parallelisation
says: splits tests across several workers or machines to cut wall-clock time
exposes hidden shared state between tests
cards.use: have a suite that takes far too long to run on one machine

cards.subject: Test impact analysis
says: runs only the tests affected by the changed code
risks missing a test if the dependency map is wrong
cards.use: want a pull request to run only the tests its change can affect

cards.subject: Flaky test quarantine
says: moves an unreliable test out of the blocking path while it is fixed
keeps the test visible and tracked rather than deleting it quietly
cards.use: have a test that fails at random and blocks everyone's merge

cards.subject: Automatic test retry
says: reruns a failed test to see whether it passes
can hide flakiness if the retries are not counted and reported
cards.use: are tempted to rerun red builds until they go green

cards.subject: A nightly full run
says: runs the slow, complete suite on a schedule rather than on every commit
gives broad coverage without slowing each pull request
cards.use: have slow end-to-end tests that are too heavy for every commit

cards.subject: A test report artifact
says: publishes results, logs and screenshots from a run so failures can be diagnosed
commonly uses a standard result format such as JUnit XML
cards.use: find a red build and cannot tell why it failed after the runner is gone

cards.subject: Building once and promoting the same artifact
says: tests the exact build that is later released
avoids a rebuild between staging and production that could change behaviour
cards.use: want to be sure production runs the very bytes that passed testing

cards.subject: ggmoney's bin/deploy.sh
says: runs all of the test scripts before deploying
refuses to upload anything if one of them fails
cards.use: want to know how ggmoney stops a broken build reaching customers
not: uploads anyway and logs a warning when a test fails

cards.subject: ggmoney's tests folder
says: holds separate scripts for VAT, payroll, banking, compliance and CSRF
also holds a tests/stress folder of scenario runs for areas such as VAT, payroll and security
cards.use: want to see where ggmoney concentrates its testing effort

cards.subject: ggmoney's csrf_test.php
says: is a regression test born from a bug in which a JSON endpoint sent its CSRF token in a header
guards against the check reading only a form field, which had stopped every VAT submission
cards.use: want an example of a regression test that came from a production bug

cards.subject: ggsocial's deploy script
says: type-checks, lints and runs npm test before shipping
has a documented emergency override
cards.use: want to know what ggsocial checks before it ships

cards.subject: SKIP_TESTS=1
says: is the documented emergency override in ggsocial's deploy script
skips the test step so an urgent fix can ship
cards.use: must ship an urgent ggsocial fix and the test step cannot run
not: is the normal way to speed up every ggsocial deploy

cards.subject: ggsocial's Vitest config
says: runs tests matching tests/**/*.test.ts in a node environment
stubs the server-only module that otherwise throws outside a Next build
cards.use: want to know how ggsocial runs server code in tests

cards.subject: GGLearn's missing test script
says: is the gap that package.json still has no test script
was first noted by the repo's earlier security review
cards.use: want to know what automated testing GGLearn lacks today

cards.subject: check:dynamic
says: re-derives each dynamic quiz answer by really running node, python, php, sqlite, git, npm semver and the TypeScript compiler
fails on any mismatch, acting as an independent oracle
cards.use: want to know how GGLearn proves its generated answers are right
not: asks a reviewer to approve each answer by hand

cards.subject: Dynamic families with no executable oracle
says: get only a structure check, such as CSS maths or REST rules
must be reviewed by hand when changed
cards.use: change a quiz family that nothing can actually execute

cards.subject: GGLearn's coverage script
says: reports how many distinct questions a learner can be asked for each track and level
takes --min and --fail options so a build can fail when a level is too thin
cards.use: want to know whether any track or level has too few questions

cards.subject: PM2's max_memory_restart
says: is set to 400M in GGLearn's ecosystem.config.cjs
is a safety net for memory growth, not a fix for a leak
cards.use: want to know what GGLearn does when a process grows too large

cards.subject: GGLearn's asynchronous password hashing
says: replaced synchronous hashing that the review flagged
avoids stalling the whole Node process under a flood of logins
cards.use: want to know why GGLearn's password hashing is not synchronous

cards.subject: GGLearn's components
says: mark decorative SVGs with aria-hidden
give the flashcard button an aria-label
cards.use: want to see GGLearn's accessibility practices in its components

qa.q: In a typical test pyramid, which kind of test should there be the most of?
qa.right: Unit tests
wrong: End-to-end tests
Manual exploratory sessions
Load tests
qa.why: Unit tests are the fastest and cheapest, so they form the wide base.

qa.q: What does a regression test protect against?
qa.right: A change breaking behaviour that used to work
wrong: A feature that was never built
Slow page loads under heavy traffic
A tester missing a deadline
qa.why: Regression tests rerun known behaviour after changes.

qa.q: Which pair of ages are the boundary values for this check?
qa.right: 17 and 18
wrong: 0 and 100
10 and 25
30 and 40
qa.why: The rule flips between 17 and 18, so boundary analysis tests both sides of that edge.

qa.q: A typo in the company name appears in the header of the home page. It breaks nothing. How would you rate it?
qa.right: Low severity, high priority
wrong: High severity, low priority
High severity, high priority
Low severity, low priority
qa.why: Impact is tiny but the business wants it fixed quickly, so severity and priority differ.

qa.q: Tests pass when run one at a time but fail when the whole suite runs. What should you look for first?
qa.right: Shared state or order dependence between tests
wrong: A longer overall suite timeout
A way to retry each failing test
A reason to delete the failing tests
qa.why: Passing alone and failing together points to tests sharing state.

qa.q: A smoke test fails right after a deployment. What is the sensible next step?
qa.right: Stop deeper testing and investigate or roll back the build
wrong: Run the full regression suite to collect more failures
Mark the build as passed and log the issue for later
Disable the smoke test for this release
qa.why: A smoke test exists to say the build is not worth testing further.

qa.q: What kind of test double is rates in this code?
qa.right: A stub, because it returns a canned value
wrong: A mock, because it verifies calls
A spy, because it records its arguments
A fake, because it stores real data
qa.why: It only returns a fixed answer to control the input; nothing is verified or recorded.

qa.q: What is this test verifying?
qa.right: That notify sent exactly one message through the send function
wrong: That notify returns the number 1
That the real mail server accepted the message
That notify finishes in under a second
qa.why: The mock's call count is the behaviour being verified.

qa.q: What happens when this test runs?
qa.right: It fails, because the floating point sum is not exactly 0.3
wrong: It passes, because 0.1 + 0.2 equals 0.3
It throws a TypeError
It passes only in Node, not in a browser
qa.why: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, so use a tolerance such as toBeCloseTo.

qa.q: A suite shows 90 percent line coverage, yet bugs keep escaping. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Check whether the tests assert outcomes, for example with mutation testing
wrong: Raise the coverage target to 100 percent
Exclude untested files from the coverage report
Add end-to-end tests for every page
qa.why: Coverage shows code ran, not that results were checked.

qa.q: A discount applies only if the customer is a member and the order is over 50. How many rules does a full decision table for these two yes or no conditions have?
qa.why: Two binary conditions give 2 x 2 = 4 combinations.

qa.q: A field accepts whole numbers from 1 to 100. At minimum, how many equivalence classes are there?
qa.why: Below the range, within it, and above it.

qa.q: Which values best cover the boundaries of a field that accepts 1 to 100?
qa.why: Boundary analysis tests on and just outside each edge.

qa.q: An end-to-end test fails about one run in ten. The team wraps it in three automatic retries. What is the main risk?
qa.right: The retries hide a real cause, so it is never found
wrong: Retries make the test slower than a unit test
Retries can only be used in unit tests
There is no risk, because retries are standard practice
qa.why: Retries without counting or investigating turn flakiness into silent noise.

qa.q: A load test reports a 200 ms average response time, but customers say the site is slow. What should you examine?
qa.right: Percentiles such as p95 and p99, because averages hide slow tails
wrong: The unit test coverage report
Whether the test ran with fewer users
The mean once more over a longer period
qa.why: A small share of very slow requests barely moves the mean but users feel them.

qa.q: A release passes staging but fails in production because a setting differs. What is the best long-term fix?
qa.right: Define environments as code and promote the same build through them
wrong: Skip staging in future
Add more unit tests that read the staging config
Test only in production
qa.why: The cause is environment drift; shared definitions and one artifact reduce it.

qa.q: A checkout flow uses a payment provider whose sandbox is rate limited. What is a sound approach?
qa.right: Stub or virtualise the provider for most tests and keep a few sandbox checks
wrong: Call the live provider with real cards in every test
Skip testing the payment step
Replace the database with a mock
qa.why: Isolating most tests from the provider keeps them fast and reliable, with a few real checks for fidelity.

qa.q: What is the main point of writing the test first in TDD?
qa.right: It shows the test can fail and defines the behaviour before the code exists
wrong: It guarantees 100 percent coverage
It lets QA sign off before development
It records known defects
qa.why: A test never seen failing might not detect anything.

qa.q: What is this text an example of?
qa.right: A BDD scenario in Given-When-Then form
wrong: A property-based test
A load test script
A mutation testing configuration
qa.why: Given, When and Then are the structure of Gherkin scenarios.
qa.code:
Given a member with a cart total of 60
When they check out
Then a 10% discount is applied

qa.q: What is the main reliability problem with this test?
qa.right: The fixed two-second sleep fails on slow runs and wastes time on fast ones
wrong: The click happens before the assertion
textContent is asynchronous
Toasts can only be tested at unit level
qa.why: Waiting for the toast element itself removes the guess.

qa.q: How should you make this function testable for expiry?
qa.right: Pass in the current time or use a fake clock
wrong: Sleep in the test until the token expires
Set exp to a random number
Run the test only at midnight
qa.why: Controlling time removes the dependence on the real clock.

qa.q: What is wrong with these two tests?
qa.right: test_b depends on whether test_a ran first because of shared mutable state
wrong: test_a should use assertEqual
Lists cannot be shared between tests
Both tests should be one test
qa.why: items is module-level, so test_a changes what test_b sees.

qa.q: A crash occurs in a feature scheduled for removal next week. How would you classify it?
qa.right: High severity, low priority
wrong: Low severity, high priority
High severity, high priority
Low severity, low priority
qa.why: The impact is serious but the business urgency is low.

qa.q: What does a good bug report contain?
qa.right: Steps to reproduce, expected result, actual result and the environment
wrong: Only a screenshot
A guess at the culprit commit and nothing else
A one-line title saying it is broken
qa.why: Others must be able to reproduce and understand the problem.

qa.q: A defect is found in production. What is the strongest response?
qa.right: Write a test that reproduces it, fix it, and ask why existing tests missed it
wrong: Fix it quickly and skip the test since it was a one-off
Add automatic retries to the suite
Raise the coverage target to 100 percent
qa.why: A regression test plus root cause analysis stops the class of problem returning.

qa.q: Which security technique examines source code without running the application?
qa.right: Static application security testing
wrong: Dynamic application security testing
A penetration test
Fuzzing
qa.why: SAST analyses code at rest.

qa.q: A security scan reports 300 findings. What should the team do first?
qa.right: Triage by exploitability and impact and fix the highest risks first
wrong: Fix them in the order listed
Turn the scanner off
Mark them all as false positives
qa.why: Triage focuses scarce time on what attackers could really use.

qa.q: A manager calls the offboard endpoint for an admin. Which status is the best expectation?
qa.why: The caller is authenticated but not permitted, which is 403 Forbidden.

qa.q: An automated accessibility scanner reports zero issues. Can you call the page accessible?
qa.right: No, scanners find only some problems, so add keyboard and screen reader checks
wrong: Yes, zero issues means fully accessible
Yes, if the scan ran on mobile
No, but only because scanners are always wrong
qa.why: Many accessibility problems need human judgment to detect.

qa.q: How do you fix this button for screen reader users?
qa.right: Add an aria-label to the button and aria-hidden to the icon
wrong: Add a title attribute to the body
Set tabindex to -1
Add an alt attribute to the button
qa.why: The button needs an accessible name, and the icon would add noise.

qa.q: What alt value is right for a purely decorative image?
qa.right: An empty alt attribute
wrong: alt="image"
alt="decorative image"
No alt attribute at all
qa.why: Empty alt tells assistive technology to skip it; a missing attribute may make it read the filename.

qa.q: What is the minimum WCAG AA contrast ratio for normal body text?
wrong: 3 to 1
7 to 1
2 to 1
qa.why: 3 to 1 is for large text and 7 to 1 is the AAA level.

qa.q: Which test is best for finding a memory leak that appears after days?
qa.right: A soak test
wrong: A spike test
A smoke test
A usability test
qa.why: Long steady load exposes slow resource growth.

qa.q: Marketing will email a million customers at noon. Which test fits best?
qa.right: A spike test
wrong: A soak test
A usability test
A snapshot test
qa.why: The risk is a sudden burst of traffic.

qa.q: A team wants to load test a new checkout during business hours in production. What is the best approach?
qa.right: Use a production-like environment or off-peak window with test accounts and safeguards
wrong: Run it at peak for realism
Never load test
Use real customers' accounts
qa.why: Load must not endanger real users or their data.

qa.q: Which is a typical exit criterion for a test cycle?
qa.right: No open critical defects and the agreed pass rate reached
wrong: A stable build is available
Every developer has gone home
The test plan has been written
qa.why: Exit criteria define when testing may stop; build availability is an entry criterion.

qa.q: It is Friday and the release has two open medium defects with workarounds. Pressure to ship is high. What is the best course?
qa.right: List them as known issues and get an explicit go/no-go decision from stakeholders
wrong: Ship and say nothing
Delay until there are zero defects, however long
Reclassify them as low so the gate passes
qa.why: The risk is accepted openly, with evidence, by those accountable.

qa.q: Developers use the emergency test override on most deploys. What should the team do?
qa.right: Treat it as a process problem: find why the gate is slow or flaky, fix it and track each override
wrong: Remove the gate so the override is unneeded
Stop asking for a reason when it is used
Nothing, since overrides are by design
qa.why: Frequent overrides signal an untrusted gate.

qa.q: What does ggmoney's csrf_test.php illustrate?
qa.right: A regression test written after a production bug and kept so it cannot return
wrong: A load test of the VAT module
A snapshot test of the user interface
A replacement for code review
qa.why: Its header describes the bug where a header token was not read by the check.

qa.q: What does GGLearn's check:dynamic use to verify answers?
qa.right: It really runs node, python, php, sqlite, git, npm semver and the TypeScript compiler
wrong: It rereads the stored answer key
It asks a model to vote on each answer
It compares against last release's output
qa.why: Executing the real tools gives an independent source of truth.

qa.q: What does ggmoney's bin/deploy.sh do when a test script fails?
qa.right: Refuses to upload anything
wrong: Uploads anyway and logs a warning
Skips only that area
Retries the test three times and continues
qa.why: Failing tests stop the deploy.

qa.q: GGLearn has no test script in package.json. What is a sound first move?
qa.right: Test the riskiest logic first, such as session and permission rules, and make failures block the pipeline
wrong: Aim for 100 percent coverage before anything else
Rely on check:dynamic alone as the test suite
Write end-to-end tests for every page first
qa.why: Risk-based effort plus a gate that stops releases gives the most value early.

qa.q: Why does ggsocial's Vitest config stub the server-only module?
qa.right: It throws outside a Next build, so tests would crash on import
wrong: It speeds up the browser
It hides failing tests
It is required by the TypeScript compiler
qa.why: The stub lets server code load in a plain node test environment.

qa.q: A process under PM2 restarts at 400M. Is the memory problem solved?
qa.right: No, it is a safety net and the leak still needs finding, for example with a soak test
wrong: Yes, restarts remove the need for further work
Yes, as long as it restarts quickly
No, because PM2 cannot restart processes
qa.why: A restart cap contains the damage but does not fix the cause.

qa.q: What does this setup do?
qa.right: Keeps tests isolated by undoing each test's database writes
wrong: Commits every test's data permanently
Speeds up the suite by disabling assertions
Seeds the production database
qa.why: Rolling back after each test leaves a clean database.

qa.q: What will line coverage and mutation testing report for this test?
qa.right: 100 percent line coverage, but the mutation that changes a + b to a - b survives
wrong: 0 percent coverage and all mutants killed
100 percent coverage and all mutants killed
The test fails because it has no assertion
qa.why: The code runs but nothing checks its result, so a mutant is not detected.

qa.q: Which property is most suited to a property-based test of a sort function?
qa.right: Sorting the output again gives the same list
wrong: The output equals [1, 2, 3] for the input [3, 1, 2]
The output is shorter than the input
The first element is unchanged
qa.why: Idempotence holds for any input, so generated inputs can check it.

qa.q: Test selection skipped the tests that a config file change should have triggered, and a bug escaped. What is the right fix?
qa.right: Treat unmapped file changes as run everything, and keep a nightly full run
wrong: Abandon test selection and run only end-to-end tests
Add the config file to the ignore list
Raise the coverage target
qa.why: Selection must fail safe when the dependency map has gaps.

qa.q: Parallelising a suite from 40 to 8 minutes causes 12 tests to fail intermittently. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: Hidden shared state or resource contention, such as ports, files or database rows
wrong: Parallel runners are inherently broken
The tests were fine and the failures are random
The suite needs fixed sleeps
qa.why: Parallel runs expose tests that were secretly relying on shared resources.

qa.q: For three parameters with three values each, what is the minimum number of tests for pairwise coverage?
qa.why: Two parameters alone have 9 value pairs, and each test covers one such pair, so at least 9 tests are needed.

qa.q: A coverage target of 90 percent is enforced, and developers start adding tests with no assertions. Which principle explains this?
qa.right: Goodhart's law: a measure that becomes a target stops being a good measure
wrong: Pareto's law: most defects come from few modules
Brooks's law: adding people slows a late project
Moore's law: hardware doubles regularly
qa.why: Pair coverage with mutation score and review.

qa.q: Developers refresh snapshot tests with the update flag whenever they fail. What does this cause?
qa.right: The snapshots stop verifying anything, so diffs must be reviewed
wrong: Faster tests with the same safety
Higher mutation scores
Less need for code review
qa.why: Blindly updating bakes in regressions.

qa.q: An end-to-end suite takes three hours and every pull request waits. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Push checks down to unit and integration tests and keep end-to-end tests for critical journeys
wrong: Add more end-to-end tests
Retry failures automatically
Run it less often and never on pull requests
qa.why: The inverted pyramid is slow and fragile.

qa.q: Which is the best exploratory charter?
qa.right: Explore checkout with expired and declined cards to find error-handling problems
wrong: Click everything for a day
Run scripted cases TC-101 to TC-150
Check that the build compiles
qa.why: A charter gives a mission without prescribing steps.

qa.q: A 5 percent canary shows the error rate doubling. What should you do?
qa.right: Halt the rollout, roll back or switch the flag off, and investigate
wrong: Increase to 50 percent for more data
Wait until the rollout finishes, then compare
Ignore it, because 5 percent is small
qa.why: A canary exists to catch problems cheaply.

qa.q: A team wants production-like data in staging. What is the best choice?
qa.right: Masked or synthetic data
wrong: A raw copy of production data
Production data with only the surnames removed
Empty tables only
qa.why: It protects real people while keeping realistic shape.

qa.q: What is wrong with this test?
qa.right: It does not wait for the promise, so it can pass before the assertion runs
wrong: toBe should be toEqual
It needs a sleep
then cannot be used in tests
qa.why: Return or await the promise so the runner waits.

qa.q: When does this test pass?
qa.right: When parse_age raises a ValueError
wrong: When parse_age returns None
When parse_age raises any other exception type
When parse_age never raises
qa.why: pytest.raises passes only if the expected exception type is raised.

qa.q: Which statement about test oracles is correct?
qa.right: A test is only as good as the independent source of expected results it uses
wrong: The code under test is always a valid oracle
Coverage numbers act as oracle
Oracles are needed only for UI tests
qa.why: Using the code's own output as the expected result proves nothing.
